title: Entrance Fee Agreement Refund Due Dates and Payment: Desk Training Questions
content:
Training material for the Resident and Family Services desk on when the refund of an **Entrance Fee Agreement** falls due and how it is paid.

**What decides the refund due date?** The refund due date depends on the plan. Where the plan's refund does not wait for re-occupancy, the refund is due the plan's non-contingent refund period, in calendar days, after the termination date. Where the plan's refund waits for re-occupancy, the refund is due the plan's re-occupancy refund period, in calendar days, after the date a new resident's full entrance fee for the same apartment is received, but never later than the plan's long-stop period, in calendar months, after the termination date, whichever is earlier; until the apartment is re-occupied the refund due date is the long-stop date.

**How are calendar months added?** Calendar months are added to the termination date keeping the day number, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist.

**What must be on file before an estate is paid?** A refund payable to an estate, where the plan requires estate documents, may be paid only after letters testamentary or letters of administration are on file, shown by the date the letters were received on the agreement; the refund is then paid to the estate's personal representative named in them.

**How many payments, and in which statuses?** Each agreement is refunded in one payment, and refunds may be paid only while the agreement is in rescinded, cancelled or refund scheduled status.

**When does the agreement close?**

> Retired clause, no longer in force: "The agreement is closed once the refund is paid and the refundable balance is 0.00." It is superseded by the current basis for closing an agreement on payment of its refund.

**Can a family ask to have a refund paid early?** A refund that is not yet due is never advanced on request; families asking to accelerate a contingent refund are told the due date the rule produces.

## Long-stop arithmetic (hypothetical termination dates, a 24 month long-stop)

| Termination date | Long-stop date |
|---|---|
| 15 June 2024 | 15 June 2026 |
| 29 February 2024 | 28 February 2026 (no 29 February in 2026) |

## Contingent due date (hypothetical, 30 day re-occupancy period, termination 15 June 2024)

| Re-occupancy record | Due date |
|---|---|
| New resident's full entrance fee received 1 March 2025 | 31 March 2025, earlier than the long-stop |
| New resident's full entrance fee received 1 June 2026 | 15 June 2026, the long-stop being earlier than 1 July 2026 |
| Not yet re-occupied | 15 June 2026, the long-stop date |

superseded_clauses: The agreement is closed once the refund is paid and the refundable balance is 0.00.
